sentences.text:
Ggudimetla Koteswararao, vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh, on
24 October, 2019

Author: Kongara Vijaya Lakshmi
Bench: Kongara Vijaya Lakshmi
 Hon'Ble Smt Justice Kongara Vijaya Lakshmi
 Criminal Petition No.6382 of 2019
Order:
 This Criminal Petition, under Section 482 of Code of Criminal
Procedure, 1973, is filed seeking to quash the proceedings against the
petitioners, who are A1 and A2, in Crime No. 266 of 2019 on the file of
Kothapet Police Station, Guntur Urban, registered for the offences
punishable under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328 and 420 read with 34 Ipc
and Sections 58, 59, 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioners and learned Public
Prosecutor.

Learned counsel for the petitioners while denying the FIR allegations would submit that even if the prosecution case is accepted to be true, tobacco products would not fall within the definition of Section 3(j) of FSS Act and therefore the police are not authorized to register the crime, investigate and file charge sheet and therefore registration of the FIR is contrary to the provisions of FSS Act.
He relied upon the common order of this Court in Criminal Petition Nos.3731 of 2018 and batch, dated 27.08.2018 .
As can be seen, in the said common order a learned Judge of this Court partly allowed the Criminal Petitions and quashed the offences punishable under Indian Penal Code and FSS Act.

sentences.text: So far as the offence under Section 188 of IPC is concerned as per Section 195(1)(a)(i) of Cr.P.C., no Court shall take cognizance of the said offence except on the complaint in writing of that Court or by such Officer of the Court as that Court may authorize in writing in this behalf, or of some other Court to which that Court is subordinate.
However, in the instant case, the FIR is registered suo moto on the report of the Sub- Inspector of Police, Kothapet Police Station.
Therefore, it is violation of Section 195 of Cr.P.C so far as the Section 188 of IC is concerned, and therefore, the said offence is also liable to be quashed.

As regards, the offence under Section 328 IPC is concerned, the learned counsel relies on the judgment of the Bombay High Court, wherein the Court held that manufacturing and possession of Gutka and Pan Masala would not amount to administering poison by any stretch of imagination.

Following the above order and for the reasons recorded therein, this Criminal Petition is allowed and the proceedings initiated against the petitioners/A1 and A2 in Crime No. 266 of 2019 on the file of Kothapet Police Station, Guntur Urban, for the offences under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328 and 420 read with 34 IPC and Sections 58, 59, 63 of Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 are hereby quashed.

As a sequel, miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this case shall stand closed.
_____________________________ KONGARA VIJAYA LAKSHMI, J Date:24.10.2019
